$comment: Canonical structured source for get-connection-details. Draft v0.3. Prose in docs/sql-server-to-azure-migration-connectivity.md is written FROM this file, never the reverse. Each row carries a source and a quote matched against the live page. That is the floor, not a guarantee: a quote proves the cell it supports, not the whole row, not the scope of the claim, and not that the page has no later section qualifying it. An external audit of v0.2 found three material errors that had all passed as verified for exactly that reason - see contradictions[v02-verification-overclaim]. Agreement between research runs is never used as evidence; anything unquotable is listed in open_research instead of being stated.

vocabulary.$comment: entra-default, entra-service-principal-certificate and entra-workload-identity were added during the merge. The original research vocabulary omitted them, yet entra-default is the mode both SqlClient and JDBC document most prominently. It is NOT a synonym for managed identity: it is a credential chain that also covers developer tooling and the CLI.

endpoints.quote: Traffic from your SQL clients to the SQL managed instance must be permitted on port 1433 across the instance's subnet address range.
endpoints.$comment: v0.3 recorded 1433-only as settled and dismissed a research run that said otherwise. An external audit quotes a page stating 1433 and 11000-11999 with a note that the range remains authoritative until further notice; that text was not located on the three pages read here. Guidance is set to the safe side because the risk is asymmetric: recommending 1433 only and being wrong fails the connection, recommending both and being wrong opens unused ports inside the customer subnet.
